obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule notification event (unauthorized acquisition of unencrypted customer information)
deadline: As soon as possible, no later than 30 days after discovery; only if 500+ consumers
notify: FTC via online form at ftc.gov

obligation: Form 8-K Item 1.05 material cybersecurity incident disclosure
deadline: Within four business days after determining the incident is material

obligation: State data breach notification (Florida worked example)
citation: Fla. Stat. 501.171(3)-(5). Each other state where affected residents live applies its own statute (not reviewed here)
trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents
deadline: Individuals: as expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred (15 more days if good cause is given in writing to the department within 30 days). Department of Legal Affairs: no later than 30 days, if 500 or more Floridians. Consumer reporting agencies: without unreasonable delay, if more than 1,000 individuals
notify: Affected Florida residents; Florida Department of Legal Affairs (500 or more); nationwide consumer reporting agencies (more than 1,000)

citation: Visa Core Rules and Visa Product and Service Rules (18 April 2026), rules 10.3.1.1 and 10.3.1.2; Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0 (effective 2026-06-25), Sections A.1-A.3 and A.5. Applied to the merchant through the acquirer's merchant agreement - not law. Other brands' rules not verified
trigger: Suspected or confirmed loss, theft, compromise or misuse of Visa account or cardholder information, including at a Member's merchants
deadline: Tell the acquirer immediately (A.3.1). Make sure the event is reported to Visa within 3 calendar days of the suspicion or confirmation (A.1.1; Core Rule 10.3.1.2 requires reporting as described in that guide), then send the incident report within 3 calendar days of that notice (A.2.1). If Visa requires a PCI Forensic Investigator, retain one within 5 business days (A.5.1.1)
notify: Acquiring bank (the Visa Member), which reports to Visa; in the US a merchant may report on the Member's behalf. Visa may require an investigation with access for a PCI Forensic Investigator (rule 10.3.1.1)
